Make unregister remove every implementation owned by the plugin while preserving implementation ordering for other plugins, and make `get_hookcallers` return each affected HookCaller exactly once. Add focused regressions covering multiple implementations on one hook and a plugin spanning more than one hook.

+def test_unregister_plugin_with_multi_hookimpls(pm: PluginManager) -> None:
+    class Hooks:
+        @hookspec
+        def he_method1(self): ...
+
+        @hookspec
+        def he_method2(self): ...
+
+    pm.add_hookspecs(Hooks)
+
+    class Plugin:
+        @hookimpl(specname="he_method1")
+        def first(self): ...
+
+        @hookimpl(specname="he_method1")
+        def second(self): ...
+
+        @hookimpl
+        def he_method2(self): ...
+
+    class OtherPlugin:
+        @hookimpl
+        def he_method1(self): ...
+
+    plugin = Plugin()
+    other_plugin = OtherPlugin()
+    pm.register(plugin)
+    pm.register(other_plugin)
+
+    hookcallers = pm.get_hookcallers(plugin)
+    assert hookcallers is not None
+    assert hookcallers == [pm.hook.he_method1, pm.hook.he_method1, pm.hook.he_method2]
+    assert len(set(hookcallers)) == 2
+
+    pm.unregister(plugin)
+
+    assert [impl.plugin for impl in pm.hook.he_method1.get_hookimpls()] == [
+        other_plugin
+    ]
+    assert pm.hook.he_method2.get_hookimpls() == []
+
+
 def test_add_hookspecs_nohooks(pm: PluginManager) -> None:
